action: Confirm technician clients run ScreenConnect 26.6.5 or later, disable RMM+ extension 1.0.31 and 1.0.32, review Run Command history, and check endpoints for a second ScreenConnect client. Do not connect to suspect hosts through ScreenConnect.
exec: Hundreds of managed endpoints were hit through a faulty third-party add-on; the feared spread to IT providers' own machines has not been observed.
plain: Attackers pushed fake copies of ConnectWise ScreenConnect remote-support software to hundreds of computers. Their toolkit tries to jump to IT technicians' machines, but researchers have not seen that step work.

key_findings: Huntress saw rogue ScreenConnect clients pushed to at least 288 hosts at 48 organisations on November 11 and 205 hosts at 41 organisations in a second wave on November 13.
Operators used the Run Command feature on cloud-hosted ScreenConnect panels to run commands as SYSTEM; one panel alone reached 190 downstream clients.
Entry appears tied to the third-party RMM+ extension, versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32, which accepted a blank access key; ConnectWise disabled five extensions across 400+ partner environments.
SCKit is 16 scripts and config files that install a rogue client, hijack the real client's connection and try to steal technician session cookies using CVE-2026-84869.
Huntress has not seen the jump from an infected endpoint to a technician workstation succeed in any recovered log.
recommendations: Verify every technician client runs ScreenConnect 26.6.5 or later and disable the affected RMM+ extension versions.
Review Run Command and Toolbox history for unexpected mass activity and check endpoints for a second, unauthorised ScreenConnect client.
Do not connect to a suspected host through ScreenConnect; use WinRM or another out-of-band tool and isolate it until cleaned.
Remove the rogue client service, the TrapWatch scheduled task and the RelayTrap folder, then rotate ScreenConnect credentials and end web sessions from a clean device.

summary: Huntress reports two waves of attacks, on November 11 and 13, in which operators used ScreenConnect's Run Command feature to install rogue clients on 288 and then 205 hosts. Entry appears linked to a flawed third-party RMM+ extension. The SCKit toolkit tries to reach technician workstations through CVE-2026-84869, but Huntress has not seen that step succeed. Technician client 26.6.5 or later fixes the flaw.
title: ConnectWise warns ScreenConnect attacks continue as SCKit spreads to MSP technicians

validation.note: Reviewed against the original Huntress report. ConnectWise's advisories page was then read in full: its newest entry is the Cloud Backup notice updated November 4, with no November notice on the ScreenConnect attacks; the separate security bulletins list did not render.
